About This Book

This phonics and spelling workbook belongs to Crystal Heights International School. It was prepared by the school’s Phonics Team to support systematic reading, spelling and vocabulary development for Grade 6 learners.

The materials are intended for use by teachers, parents and students of Crystal Heights International School. They form part of the school’s structured literacy programme and are not the work of any single individual.

We hope these pages help every child grow in confidence as a reader and writer.


How to Use This Book

Every unit covers 7 stages. Stages 1 and 2 (Word List and Word Sort) share one combined page; Stages 3–7 each get their own page. A 7-dot progress bar appears at the top of every lesson page, and each stage keeps its own fixed color, so you always know exactly which stage you are on.

📋 Stage 1: Word List
🗂 Stage 2: Word Sort
📖 Stage 3: Word Meaning
🗣 Stage 4: Reading Fluency
✏ Stage 5: Proofreading
🧩 Stage 6: Phonetic & Decoding
✍ Stage 7: Working Space

Review pages follow Units 4, 8 and 12, and a Final Review closes the book. The answer keys, glossary and index of sounds are at the back.

Key Ideas
  • Double consonants often follow a short vowel sound: middle, sudden, common, supper.
  • The doubled letters usually make a single sound, not two.
  • In a few compound words, the double letters may make two sounds (fishhook, bookkeeper). These are rare.

Reading Fluency — Unit 1

Read the passage aloud. Then find and circle every word that uses this unit’s pattern.

The Long Walk Home

The traffic was terrible that evening, and it was difficult to find a taxi. Kofi decided to walk. In the middle of the road, he saw an old woman carrying a heavy basket. "May I help you?" he asked. "It is no struggle for me." She smiled. "You are an excellent young man," she said. They walked together until they reached her house. "Come in for supper," she offered. Kofi looked in the mirror by the door. "I would not recommend it tonight," he said. And with a sudden burst of energy, he continued his walk.

Now read it again, aiming for a smooth, natural pace.

The Village Clinic

The village clinic is small but decent. It offers a necessary service to everyone. On the surface, it may not look modern, but inside there is medicine, clean water, and a place to exercise. Each year the villagers celebrate the doctor's birthday with silence and respect, then burst into song. What is the difference between this clinic and a big city hospital? Here, everyone knows your name.

The Young Architect

Adwoa had the character of a real scientist, but her heart belonged to buildings. After school she would visit the local mechanic, who taught her the technique of fixing engines. "You have a gift," he said, rubbing his aching stomach. One evening, an orchestra came to her town. In the chaos of setting up the stage, the conductor dropped his baton near a clump of antique tiles. Adwoa quietly picked it up. The audience broke into applause. From that day her name was a kind of chronic legend in her small town.

Now read it again, aiming for a smooth, natural pace.

The Bridge on the Journey

On a long journey through the mountains, a generous farmer stopped his engine at a narrow bridge. A young girl had fallen and hurt her leg. "This is an urgent injury," the farmer said. "We must act at once." He adjusted his jacket, imagined the safest route, and carried her across. The majority of the villagers later gave him a badge of honour. His only pledge was this: never dodge a chance to help.

Review 1 — Mixed Context Word Bank
difficult (double f), excellent (double l), common (double m), celebrate (c spells /s/), necessary (s+c spells /s/), surface (c spells /s/), chemist (ch spells /k/), technique (qu spells /k/), antique (qu spells /k/), journey (j spells /j/), generous (g before e), knowledge (dge spells /j/). Pupils' sentences will vary. Accept any sentence that correctly uses a Mixed Word Store word with its target pattern underlined.

Review 2 — Mixed Context Word Bank
audience (au spells /o/), laundry (au spells /o/), flawless (aw spells /o/), morning (or), court (our), board (oar), amount (ou), moisture (ou), employ (oi), rhythm (silent h), castle (silent t), island (silent s). Pupils' sentences will vary. Accept any sentence that correctly uses a Mixed Word Store word with its target pattern underlined.

Review 3 — Mixed Context Word Bank
vegetable (schwa), elephant (schwa), mystery (schwa), running (doubled n), preferred (doubled r), beginning (doubled n), hoping (dropped e), writing (dropped e), dangerous (dropped e), peaceful (kept e), movement (kept e), excitement (kept e). Pupils' sentences will vary. Accept any sentence that correctly uses a Mixed Word Store word with its target pattern underlined.

Notes on Sort Criteria
Different patterns use different sorting criteria. Use the criterion that genuinely divides the words into meaningful groups:
• Spelling-letter grouping (Units 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 13): sort by which letter or letters spell the target sound.
• Alphabetical order (Units 1, 8, 9): used when the words share the same sound or rule and cannot be split into meaningful sound groups. This also teaches dictionary skills.
• Word analysis (Units 10, 11, 12): sort by which suffix or spelling rule applies.

pages.name: Glossary
pages.subtitle: KEY TERMS
pages.html:
Glossary
TermMeaning
ConsonantAny letter of the alphabet other than a, e, i, o, u.
DecodingUsing knowledge of letter sounds to read a word.
DiphthongTwo vowels that make a new sound when combined (oi, ow).
PhonemeThe smallest unit of sound in a word.
PhonicsA method of teaching reading that links letters to sounds.
ProofreadTo read and correct errors in writing.
r-controlled vowelA vowel followed by r where the sound changes (park, fork, fern).
SchwaAn unstressed vowel sound, heard as a soft "uh".
Short vowelA vowel with a short sound (apple, egg, igloo, octopus, umbrella).
Silent letterA letter that is written but not pronounced (knock, island).
SuffixA group of letters added to the end of a word (-ing, -ful, -ment).
SyllableA unit of sound in a word containing one vowel sound.
Word StoreThe list of spelling words for a unit.
